messages:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing dropped spans when routing OTLP from the collector to Tempo for the payments service. Downsampled traces look incomplete.

marta: Huh. Any patterns? service.name or instrumentation library?

alex: Looks like spans with `trace.status.code` set are being dropped by the tempo-receiver when we set `attributes.action = drop` in our processor chain. Happens only when we rewrite `dataset` for honeycomb too.

samir: That sounds like the attributes processor ordering bug. We inline-set dataset and service.name for Honeycomb, then route to both exporters via `batch/queued_retry`. Tempo expects `otel.resource.attributes` to include `service.name`, not a `dataset` key.

jin: Quick context: We added a shim to add `dataset` for teams that want Honeycomb logical datasets. That shim uses the `attributes` processor:
```yaml
processors:
  attributes/shim_dataset:
    actions:
      - key: dataset
        value: "payments-prod"
        action: insert
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [attributes/shim_dataset, batch]
```

marta: The problem might be that we mutate too early, then a later processor marks spans to be dropped for Tempo due to dataset not recognized. Maybe our routing filter checks `dataset` presence as accept, but Tempo path doesn't expect it and fails mapping, so `drop` fallback triggers.

alex: Observability logs show exporter: "tempo: failed to translate span — unknown attribute dataset" then a `processor/drop` event.

observability-bot: exporter-error — tempo-exporter returned 400 for 3 spans in pipeline `traces`. See /internal/observability/trace-errors/1769876543

samir: Proposed options: 1) Use `attributes` processor only for Honeycomb exporter via `spanmetrics`/`routing` processor to set dataset per exporter. 2) Keep global attribute but add a `translate` processor before Tempo exporter to remove `dataset`. 3) Switch to separate pipelines per backend (dup payloads).

jin: Separate pipelines seems safest but doubles CPU. We should prefer in-pipeline transform: remove dataset before Tempo. Example config:
```yaml
exporters:
  tempo:
    endpoint: tempo.internal:9411
processors:
  attributes/remove_dataset:
    actions:
      - key: dataset
        action: delete
service:
  pipelines:
    traces_honeycomb:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes/shim_dataset, batch]
      exporters: [honeycomb]
    traces_tempo:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes/remove_dataset, batch]
      exporters: [tempo]
```

marta: That preserves a single OTLP receiver but duplicates pipeline CPU. Could also use `route` processor to send copies conditionally with different processors per binding — less duplication but config trickier.

alex: Also need to think retention tagging. Honeycomb datasets map to retention/cost buckets; some teams want 90d vs default 15d. We currently control retention via `dataset` name, so removing dataset for Tempo is fine, but we must ensure our billing pipeline reads dataset before we strip it.

samir: Agreed. Billing hook must run before `remove_dataset`. Order matters: attributes -> billing -> remove_dataset -> export tempo.

jin: One more gotcha: span `kind` and `status` mapping differ (Honeycomb expects `spanKind`, Tempo expects `otel.span_kind`). We added a tiny translate processor to map keys. Make sure that runs after we insert dataset but before exporter-specific removals.

alex: Action items: Samir to prototype `route`-based copy pipeline that sets dataset only on the Honeycomb copy and strips it for Tempo; Jin to add unit test with sample spans (error/status/span.kind) and run against local tempo dev; Marta to add billing preprocessor hook to ensure retention is computed pre-strip.

marta: I'll also add a short doc in eng-platform/observability about exporter-specific attribute hygiene so future teams don't mutate global attrs that other backends choke on.

ops-bot: Created ticket PF-879: "Telemetry: per-exporter dataset shim and routing; prevent span drops" assigned to samir. ETA: 2w.

alex: Sounds good. If someone wants to pair now I can demo the failing payloads.

samir: I'll join in 10.

observability-bot: note: if anyone hits 400s from tempo again, add `--collector-log-level=debug` and paste logs here. :eyes:
